dialogue_text: Ten days. I'm not asking for more than that. No.
What's going on? He's looking for a place to stay.
He's looking for a place to stay. Transmission quit on me out on the highway. Ned Granger towed it into town said you folks were short a hand.
We were short a hand three weeks ago. Our man walked. I can start this afternoon. We can't pay another hand.
I'm not asking for pay. A roof, a hot meal, and someplace warm for him. Ten days. I'm not asking for more than that.
No. Does he eat a lot? More than he lets on in the interview.
More than he lets on in the interview. That corner post how long's it been leaning like that?
That corner post how long's it been leaning like that? That's not your business. Might be in a minute.
Wren lower gate! Gunner, stay. You're not bringing him?
You're not bringing him? He's never worked cattle. He'd only make it worse. Where's this run out to?
Where's this run out to? Straight to Willow Creek. Then we head 'em off short of the ice. You've worked cows? Raised on 'em. Idaho.
Easy. Don't push 'em. I've been moving cows since I could walk.
I've been moving cows since I could walk. Then you know they don't take orders. …eleven, twelve. That's every one that got out.
Kroll. Third time this month he's just happened to drive by.
Kroll. Third time this month he's just happened to drive by. Who's Kroll? Nobody you need to worry about.
That patch won't last till morning if it freezes hard. I'll get to it in the morning. Fixing it tonight beats fishing cows out of the creek tomorrow.
Fixing it tonight beats fishing cows out of the creek tomorrow. You got a name? Cole Brandt. And that's Gunner.
Cole Brandt. And that's Gunner. He's the one who did what he was told.
Maggie Sutter. That's my sister, Wren. Hi. He just saved us a night in the creek.
He's a stranger with a duffel bag. And a dog that sits when he's told. That's more than we got out of the last guy. Supper's at six.
Supper's at six. Dog stays off the furniture. Yes, ma'am. It's just stew.
After today, anything hot is a feast. He can lie by the stove. Not on the couch.
Hear that? Best behavior. Our dad. Earl.
Our dad. Earl. We lost him in October. His heart. I'm sorry. Everybody's sorry. Doesn't fix the roof.
What else needs fixing? Hay barn roof leaks. The water line to the stock tank freezes every morning. Half the porch is rotten.
the porch is rotten. Why did your man walk? Because we owed him two months' wages. And because Kroll found him a job on the resort crew down the valley.
Double our pay. Your dad have a shop? Everything he ever owned that had a handle.
Everything he ever owned that had a handle. Then I know where I'm starting tomorrow.
Ms. Sutter, Dennis Kroll. I've raised my offer again. It stands through the end of the month. I'd hate for the bank to make this decision for you.
I'd hate for the bank to make this decision for you. That's Kroll. He bought the Henderson place down the creek last fall.
He bought the Henderson place down the creek last fall. Hasn't run a single cow on it. He'll hear it in town anyway. We're four payments behind,
We're four payments behind, and the bank wants a new payment plan by the twentieth. Ten days. The old foreman's cabin behind the barn. Thank you.
Ten days. The old foreman's cabin behind the barn. Thank you. Don't make me sorry I said yes. Fair enough.
Nobody's slept here in two years. Not since our foreman retired.
Four walls and no gearshift. That's an upgrade. That latch is shot. I'll fix it.
That latch is shot. I'll fix it. You're supposed to be resting tonight. Never got the hang of it. He seems to manage. He's had more practice.
He's had more practice. Why ten days? That's how long Ned needs to get a rebuilt transmission up from Billings. After that I'll find work somewhere north.
After that I'll find work somewhere north. "Somewhere north" is a lot of country. That's what I like about it.
Don't get attached, partner.
Nobody's moved a thing since October. May I? Go ahead. He oiled every wrench in here.
Go ahead. He oiled every wrench in here. Never once got his own heart checked. Haven't seen one of these since my dad's barn.
So you did grow up on a ranch. Idaho, till I was eighteen. Then twelve years in the Navy. Doing what? SEAL teams. And him?
Doing what? SEAL teams. And him? Military working dog. Patrol and explosives detection. When he retired, I signed the papers. He's retired?
And he's very good at it. Dad's book. Thirty years. Every repair, every calf,
Dad's book. Thirty years. Every repair, every calf, every bad winter. Might save you some guessing.
I'll take good care of it. This is Clover.
Last one still to calve this year. Any day now. She looks ready to be done with it. Don't we all.
Dad kept meaning to fix that.
"Barn side door. Latch, bottom hinge."
That'll hold in a normal wind. Not a real one.
Nothing in here fits a door this old. Feed store doesn't carry that size.
Feed store doesn't carry that size. They'll order it out of Billings. Two, three weeks. Then the wedge'll have to do till then.
Most of these are still good. No sense tearing out what still holds.
No sense tearing out what still holds. That's exactly what Dad always said. Word for word. Sounds like a man who'd paid for lumber.
Sounds like a man who'd paid for lumber. He paid for everything twice. Once in cash, once in complaining.
Fence is over here, partner.
How many SEALs does it take to fix a roof? One. If his helper quits talking.
Dry. First time since Christmas. Check it again the first night it drops below zero. Yes, sir.
Check it again the first night it drops below zero. Yes, sir. Don't salute me. I'm a civilian now. Heat tape's on a thermostat. It kicks
Heat tape's on a thermostat. It kicks on when it drops below freezing.
Dad bought this the summer before he died. Kept saying he'd paint the porch once calving was over. Nothing on a ranch ever slows down. Warm white.
Nothing on a ranch ever slows down. Warm white. Your dad had good taste. Has he done anything all day? He's supervising.
What's he doing? That side door. Wind's knocking it. Retired doesn't mean off duty.
Part's on order. Till then, the wedge holds. That was Dad's chair.
He sat there every night. Watched the light go off the mountains. Best seat on the place. I haven't sat out here since October.
Sitting in his chair doesn't mean you're taking his place.
He would've hated how long that paint sat in the basement.
He would've hated how long that paint sat in the basement. He'd like where it ended up. Thank you. For the porch. Wren did the railings. I just held a brush.
I just held a brush. Wren talked the whole time. She did.
You fixed the window. That thing let the whole winter in. Your foreman had the best window on the place.
Your foreman had the best window on the place. He said that every morning for twenty years. Folks in Denver would pay to wake up to that. What are you talking about? A guest cabin. Weekends.
A guest cabin. Weekends. People who want quiet and cows and a mountain. We raise cattle. We don't change sheets. One cabin. One set of sheets.
One cabin. One set of sheets. Ideas don't make loan payments. Neither does a cabin full of mice. I did four years at a hotel front desk in Bozeman.

I did four years at a hotel front desk in Bozeman. I know what guests want, what they break, and what they'll pay for. I'll check what the county needs to make it legal and I'll do the cleaning, the bookings,
the bookings, the breakfast baskets. Mine. Not yours. Write down what it costs. Then we decide.
We keep Grandma's quilt. Anything worth keeping, we keep.
First guest. Off the quilt. He doesn't take orders from civilians. He takes stew from one.
If the cabin books even two weekends a month, it covers the fuel and the vet bills. And the bank still wants a plan.
You've gone quiet. I'm better with fence posts than figures. That sounds like a man who's sat across from a banker.
After the Navy I bought a little place outside Twin Falls. Bought a tractor I couldn't afford.
Signed a hay contract I was sure would last. It didn't. Somebody cheat you? Nobody cheated me. I could outwork any man in the county.
I thought that was the same as running the place. It's not. Found that out the expensive way. When I went to the bank, I brought them a dream.
I brought them a dream. They didn't want a dream. They wanted to see the worst year, and how I'd live through it.
I didn't have one. Five years, and it was gone. And since then?
And since then? A year of other people's ranches. Two months here, three there. Why keep moving?
If I'm gone before a place feels like home, it doesn't hurt to go. Or maybe Gunner's tired of packing up.
Dad put everything he ever learned about this place in here. Plenty of blank pages left.
Plenty of blank pages left. You sure? Just leave his writing where it is. I wouldn't touch it. Hay barn roof. New tin,
Hay barn roof. New tin, fourteen sheets. Holds. "Holds." Dad would've liked that.
What've you got?
Easy… Okay. Go.
Show me.
"Willow Creek. Site three."
Two of them. Half-ton pickup, chains on the rear. Came up the creek from the Henderson side.
Cut it and twisted it back so nobody'd notice till spring.
In the morning. Good work, Gunner. Good work.
She runs. Part came in two days early. Cost you more than the truck's worth, but she runs. Thanks, Ned.
Thanks, Ned. Huh. It's real. One more thing. Outfit up by Havre's looking for a full-time hand. Year-round, bunkhouse,
Year-round, bunkhouse, decent wages. Starts the twentieth. I gave them your name. That's good news.
Maggie, there's something I need— Or he could stay a little longer. The cabin's not— He has somewhere to be. I should pack.
I should pack. What'd I just walk into? Nine days of something. Get your coat, Wren. We're going into town
Get your coat, Wren. We're going into town to find out what the bank wants in that plan. Now? Now.
Afternoon, ladies. Thought I'd save you a phone call. I've gone up enough to clear the bank and leave you both something to start fresh somewhere easier.
This is home. We're not shopping for another. A home that loses money every month it stands. New paint. Fence is tight. Very nice.
New paint. Fence is tight. Very nice. But paint doesn't make a payment. We're opening the cabin to guests. That's money coming in.
That's money coming in. Weekend tourists won't feed forty-two cows. Not today, Mr. Kroll.
Not today, Mr. Kroll. Your father understood numbers, Ms. Sutter. Don't tell me what my father understood.
Creek's running low this year, I hear.
"We"? What did you mean, we? I was trying to help. I know you were. This is our ranch, Cole. Wren's and mine.
Wren's and mine. Decisions here are ours to make. Patching a roof doesn't give you a say in my life.
You're right. That wasn't mine to say. I'm sorry. He wasn't after anything that's yours.
He wasn't after anything that's yours. He's the one person who actually showed up. I know. And this morning you told him he had somewhere to be. You decided for him, Maggie. Same
You decided for him, Maggie. Same thing he just did to us.
Your ranch.
Come on, Gunner. Time to go. Gunner! What is it?
Gunner! What is it? The barn.
The barn. Wind's coming straight through that door. We need to get the others away from her.
We need to get the others away from her. Clover's calving. Now. I'll call the vet.
Thought you'd be halfway to Havre by now. Not yet. Tell me what to do. Get that door shut first. Then the rest of them go to the back pen.
Wren, on three. One, two three! Drill and a two-by-six!
Keep her quiet and warm. Don't pull unless I tell you. I'm twenty minutes out.
I'm twenty minutes out. Quiet and warm. Got it. Gunner. Stay. With her.
All right, mama. Let's see what you've got.
Look at him. He made it. We all made it.
He made it. We all made it. Whoever got that door shut saved you a cow and a calf. Another hour of that wind, you'd have lost them both.
You stayed with us. That'll hold till the real parts come in.
Gunner found these on your creek Thursday night.

Gunner found these on your creek Thursday night. Two men in a half-ton came up from the Henderson side cut your fence and twisted it back. Kroll's got the same flags in his truck bed, and a crate of these
Kroll's got the same flags in his truck bed, and a crate of these bottles with number three missing. It's your ranch. Your call. C.
Why didn't you tell me?
Why didn't you tell me? I was about to. Then Ned pulled in, and you said I had somewhere to be. And that night,
you'd just told me it wasn't my say. I did say that. I'll stay till Clover and the calf are out of the woods. If that's all right with you.
If that's all right with you. Breakfast's at six. He said banks don't want a dream. They want the worst year.
Then Dad already wrote it. Thirty years of calving rates. The drought in '88. The blizzard in '97. Every year we didn't go under.
Every year we didn't go under. Sell six open cows. That catches us up on the back payments. The roof and the water line are done. No big repair bills this year.
No big repair bills this year. Budget for them anyway. Cabin income, first year zero. Zero? Worst year, Wren.
Six open cows now, or wait for fall prices? Your call. I'm asking what you think. I'm not asking you to decide.
Now. Prices are up, and it shows the bank you'll cut before they make you.
Monday, we hand it in. …thanks for your patience since Monday. The board will restructure the note. Conditions: six head sold by April first, and quarterly statements.
Conditions: six head sold by April first, and quarterly statements. But we're willing to work with you. Thank you. We'll have it done.
Is it enough? It's a shot. A fair one. Heard in town you ladies paid the bank a visit Monday.
Heard in town you ladies paid the bank a visit Monday. I take it you've decided. We have. We're declining your offer. Both of you feel that way? Both of us.
Both of you feel that way? Both of us. You're taking on a lot of risk. We know.
Did that drifter talk you into this? No. This one's ours.
Site three. The one your crate's been missing since Thursday. You found our hand a job on that resort crew at double pay. You bought the Henderson place last fall
You bought the Henderson place last fall and never ran a single cow on it. You were never buying cattle ground.
You're buying Willow Creek for that resort. Our water right on that creek goes back to 1904. Senior to everybody downstream.
Testing water isn't a crime, Ms. Sutter. Cutting my fence at midnight is. Next time anybody working for you sets foot on this place, I call the sheriff.
I call the sheriff. Water's worth more than beef in this valley. Your father knew that.
Your father knew that. He did. That's why he never sold. Offer's open if you come to your senses. We won't. Drive safe, Mr. Kroll.
You're locking me in? Two weeks ago you stood outside this gate and asked me for ten days. Now I'm the one standing at it, asking.
You've got a cabin to finish. Bank conditions. You don't need another problem to manage. You're not a problem. When I said you had somewhere to be,
that was because I couldn't pay you to stay. Since Dad, I've held on to this place so tight I wouldn't let anybody near it. Not even Wren.
I wouldn't let anybody near it. Not even Wren. I've done the same thing with a duffel bag. Wren and I want you to stay.
For real this time. The new note leaves room for one real wage. Everything in writing.
Everything in writing. And if this works, a piece of the ranch down the road. And if it doesn't work? Then we sit at that table and talk it out.
Then we sit at that table and talk it out. Nobody leaves in the night. We? We. That a job offer? Some of it.
And the rest? I'd miss you. Not half as much as I'd miss you.
Don't forget me! Couldn't if I tried! He's feeling left out!
Morning. This is Cole Brandt, about the job in Havre. I'm gonna have to turn it down. …Yes, sir. I found a place.
…Yes, sir. I found a place. But there's a Marine in Billings, just got out, best hand I know. I'll send him your way.
County signed off last week. And that's our first booking pulling in!
Strangers are actually paying to sleep here? That's kind of the point of a booking. Oh! The dog from the listing!
Oh! The dog from the listing! That's Gunner. He's supervising. Might book a weekend myself. Ned, you live ten minutes away. Exactly. No travel.
Exactly. No travel. Wages, and a cut of the profits for now. Anything about ownership goes on paper.
Anything about ownership goes on paper. Nothing on a handshake. Nothing on a handshake. Twelve years in the Navy, and I never signed this much. Sign it.
Twelve years in the Navy, and I never signed this much. Sign it. Barn side door.
New latch and hinge came in. Holds. Dad would've put you to work your first hour. Wish I'd gotten to shake his hand.
You said ten days. Never was any good at counting. How long this time? Long enough to watch that calf grow up.
Long enough to watch that calf grow up. Welcome home, Cole.
